question.problem:
In $△ABC,$ we have $m∠A={114}^{∘},$ $AC=5,$ and $BC=9.$ Which of the following statements *could* be true?

I. $∠B$ is acute

II. $m∠C={44.9}^{∘}$ rounded to one decimal place

III. $m∠B={30.5}^{∘}$ rounded to one decimal place
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/da8f9302098e74dc26c360207d9062d96ac14d17299cf5a2993d70ce45fc69b5.png)

The law of sines states that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡B}{b}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡A}{a}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
a=9,\,m∠A={114}^{∘},\,b=5,
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡B}{5} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{114}^{∘}}{9} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡B & =5\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{114}^{∘}}{9} \\  & ≈5\cdot \frac{0.913\,55}{9} \\  & ≈0.507\,53,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places.

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠B & ≈\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.507\,53)≈{30.5}^{∘},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠C & ≈{180}^{∘}-m∠A-m∠B \\  & ≈{180}^{∘}-{114}^{∘}-{30.5}^{∘} \\  & ≈{35.5}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Another solution to $\operatorname{sin}⁡B≈0.507\,53$ is given by

$$
m∠B≈{180}^{∘}-{30.5}^{∘}≈{149.5}^{∘}.
$$

But we know that a triangle cannot have two obtuse angles. Therefore, there is no triangle that has two angles whose measures are ${114}^{∘}$ and ${149.5}^{∘}.$

So, there is only one possible triangle, with the following angle measures:

$$
m∠A={114}^{∘},\,m∠B≈{30.5}^{∘},\,m∠C≈{35.5}^{∘}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/88208a1751e4af718bac2c58dac144034c6a92d9d5faaf2b9a6861b7f44f32f5.png)

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and III only."
